gaps: P0: none; P3 and P5: nothing (most hits in those periods are New Orleans); no second P4
notes: #4 is a photo of the bound book but the plate lies flat; only a faint fold line crosses the view. #9: Cleveland’s date is given as 1665; Doomer drew the Loire in 1646 and made finished sheets later, so about 1665. #25 is a tall portrait; the 16:9 crop will show only the middle of the facade, drop it if a blank plate is preferred. Not usable here but worth knowing: tours/#20 is a 1931 aerial of Orléans (Meurisse, Gallica) filed under Tours. #11–14 and #17–24 are New Orleans; #7 is a Paris garden; #10 is “near Orléans”; #26–28 are museum photos of paintings with uncertain dates.
